applies_why: The judge text decides the D1/C2 collision by treating Matthew 1:16's own grammar as admitting both readings, which is a verse-by-verse determination rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — read as requiring comparison of the two chains' overall footing, versus read as permitting a single verse to be declared underdetermined by its own grammar.
why: The judge text makes Matthew 1:16's own ambiguity decisive, so it fails to weigh the two chains by footing as K-C requires.
